_note: Administration zone. These buildings mostly enable political capability rather than producing anything — which is why they are the first thing a player under resource pressure wants to cut, and why cutting them is a trap. The archive gates the Apocrypha, and therefore the whole Chapter 2 mechanic.

buildings.name: Council chamber
buildings._note: Its repair cost is timber for chamber fittings — the ceremonial spend that buys legitimacy. Let it decay and the Accord cannot be amended at all.

buildings.name: Archive
buildings._note: Holds the Apocrypha in its restricted rear chamber, and therefore the Nexus. Also where Chapter 1's archive-record inconsistencies are found. Neglecting the archive quietly closes the story down.

buildings.name: Security post
buildings._note: The Order faction's physical footprint. Every one built trades freedom for stability at a fixed rate, which is the whole game in one building.

buildings.name: Holding cells
buildings._note: Unlocks the harsh branch of several dilemmas. Without it, 'make an example of him' is not on the menu — the buildings a player owns shape which rulings they are even offered.
